implementation_notes: Jetpack Compose supplies the hook machinery in its runtime: remember stores a value in the Composition for the next recomposition, mutableStateOf creates observable state whose reads schedule recomposition of the reading composables, rememberSaveable survives configuration changes, and derivedStateOf avoids redundant recomputation. Effects are lifecycle-scoped - LaunchedEffect launches a coroutine that is cancelled when it leaves the Composition and restarted on key change, DisposableEffect requires an onDispose block, and rememberCoroutineScope, SideEffect, produceState and rememberUpdatedState cover event-scoped and external-source cases - so the reusable unit is an ordinary @Composable function (by convention rememberSomething) returning state and callbacks. That replaces ViewModel-inheritance and mixin-style reuse; a plain class plus a StateFlow collected with collectAsStateWithLifecycle remains justified when the behaviour must outlive the composition or be shared across screens.
pitfalls: Remembered values are bound to the call site in the Composition: placing remember behind a conditional or inside a loop restarts state, and the key argument decides when LaunchedEffect/DisposableEffect cancels and restarts.
remember does not survive configuration changes or process death - use rememberSaveable for anything the user expects to persist.
State read outside composition (plain suspend code, ViewModel) does not trigger recomposition; keep observable state in State/snapshot primitives or convert a Flow with collectAsStateWithLifecycle.
